chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Should I pray the two cycles of the obligatory Tawaaf behind the Standing Place (Maqam Ibrahim) where it is at the present time, or where it was in the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Where it is at the present time.'

key_terms.حَيْثُ هُوَ السَّاعَةَ: Where it is at the present time
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two cycles of the obligatory circumambulation prayer
key_terms.عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: In the era of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: Where should the two cycles of Tawaaf prayer be performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic preference for praying the two cycles of Tawaaf behind the Maqam Ibrahim in its contemporary location rather than its historical position during the Prophet's era. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of sacred geography and the validity of current ritual practices despite historical changes in the Kaaba's structure. It serves as a practical guide for pilgrims, resolving potential confusion between historical precedent and established ritual norm.
